lines: ClipFund. An AI agent that earns its own stock treasury, on Base.
ClipFund: an AI agent that earns its own stock treasury, on Base.
This is my entry for Stocks Maxxing, track two point one.
My entry for Base Stocks Maxxing · Track 2.1
Clipping streams is repetitive work, perfect for an agent.
Clipping streams is repetitive work, a good fit for an agent.
But agent treasuries are usually a black box, and one key can spend everything.
But agent treasuries are usually a black box, and one key can spend everything.
ClipFund sells clips for fifty cents in U S D C, paid over x four oh two, straight into a treasury contract.
ClipFund sells clips for $0.50 USDC over x402, paid straight into a treasury contract.
The contract fills a locked reserve first. Then my share of the surplus buys tokenized stocks, and the rest stays as cash.
Reserve first (locked). Then an owner-set share of the surplus buys tokenized stocks. The rest stays as USDC.
All the rules live in one contract, and all thirteen Foundry tests pass.
The rules live in one contract. All 13 Foundry tests pass, including a 512-run fuzz test.
Here's the demo, on a local fork of Base Sepolia.
Live demo on a local fork of Base Sepolia (chain 84532).
Call the clip endpoint without paying, and you get four oh two, Payment Required.
POST /clip without paying → HTTP 402 Payment Required: 0.50 USDC to the treasury.
The client signs a U S D C authorization and retries. The clip comes back, the payment settles, and the agent books it.
Client signs an EIP-3009 USDC authorization → HTTP 200 + clip → settled onchain → recordPayment().
The first two payments all go to the reserve, until it hits one dollar.
Payments 1–2 go 100% to the locked reserve until it hits its $1.00 target.
After that, sixty percent of the surplus goes to stocks, and the agent buys s COIN and s N V D A.
Then 60% of surplus → stock budget → the agent buys sCOIN and sNVDA.
Each one is capped at thirty five percent of the treasury. Go over, and the buy reverts.
Each stock is capped at 35% of treasury NAV. Above the cap, the buy reverts.
Running costs come out of the reserve only, and the next payment tops it back up first.
Operating costs come from the reserve only, to an allowlisted payee. The next payment refills it first.
The dashboard rebuilds it all from on chain events. All twelve checks pass, and every payment matches a real settlement.
Rebuilt from onchain events: all 12 reconciliation checks pass, every payment matched to its x402 settlement tx.
And this is what the customer actually paid for.
What the customer paid for: a 9:16 headline clip, cut with ffmpeg.
The agent can't change the rules or withdraw. The reserve can't be invested. And payments can't be faked or counted twice.
The agent key can't change policy or withdraw. The reserve can't be invested. Payments can't be faked or booked twice.
To be clear, this is a testnet demo. No real money.
To be clear: testnet demo, local Base Sepolia fork, test USDC, no real money.
s COIN and s N V D A are simulated tokens with a fixed price, and the payment facilitator runs locally.
sCOIN / sNVDA are simulated test tokens (fixed mock price, no rights in any company). The x402 facilitator runs in-process.
Useful work, revenue, reserve, stocks. That's ClipFund.
Useful work → revenue → reserve → stock treasury.
